column1: # Macros Emacs' *own source headers* define, which config.h alone cannot decide, and which
# the frozen `#if` evaluator therefore had to be told about (tools/gen-cond-macros.py merges
# One `<header>\t<macro>` per row.  The generator measures the value with the same clang
# invocation it uses for the config.h dump (`#include <config.h>` then `#include "<header>"`
# on the frozen include paths), so a row cannot go stale silently: a header that stops
# defining the macro is reported, and a wrong value shows up as a disagreement in
# tools/check-cond-eval.py before the file joins the verified list (PORTING.md P-66).
# || defined HAVE_ITIMERSPEC)` -> `# define PROFILER_CPU_SUPPORT`.  Both SIGPROF (27) and
# HAVE_SETITIMER (1) are in the config.h table, PROFILING is not, so the macro is defined and
# profiler.c's whole CPU-profiler region (C 343-524, C 699-712) is live text - without this
# row the evaluator called it dead and the gate rejected the port's `defsubr`s as
# src/sysdep.c's terminal/ioctl/signal conditions (2026-10-03, the sysdep worker).
# The file is `<termios.h>`/`<sys/ioctl.h>`/`<syssignal.h>` text, so config.h alone cannot
# decide it: `check-cond-eval.py src/sysdep.c` reported 63 disagreements before these rows
# and 2 after (both are tools/cinventory.py's trailing-comment defect, reported in
# docs/ports/sysdep.md - the evaluator is right in both, clang's probe is ill-formed).
# sysdep.c is nevertheless NOT added to cond-eval-verified.txt: it carries both arms of
# every `#if` (status 3.49) and a verified file's checker demands only the live one
# src/process.c's socket/interface conditions (2026-10-04, the process worker).
# text, so config.h alone cannot decide it: `check-cond-eval.py src/process.c` reported 29
# disagreements before these rows.  Each row was measured by including exactly that header
# after config.h and asking clang whether the macro is then defined (the same invocation
# tools/gen-cond-macros.py uses).  src/process.c is nevertheless NOT added to
# cond-eval-verified.txt: it carries both arms of every `#if` (status 3.49), and a verified
# file's checker demands only the live one (docs/status.md 3.51's callproc.c note).
# src/font.c's FONT_DEBUG (2026-10-04, the font lane).  `src/font.h` 997-998 defines it
# (`#ifndef FONT_DEBUG` / `#define FONT_DEBUG`), so it comes from the source header and not
# from config.h: the frozen table cannot decide it and `check-cond-eval.py src/font.c`
# reported `2 disagreements` (both `#ifdef FONT_DEBUG`, C 5240/5938).  Clang measured with the
# same invocation gen-cond-macros.py uses: defined.  With the row in the table the file is 0
# disagreements, and C 5938-5949's eight `defsubr`s become live text the port transcribes
# src/lisp.h's USE_LSB_TAG (2026-10-04, the alloc lane's finding).  lisp.h 250-257 computes it
# `(VAL_MAX / 2 < INTPTR_MAX)`); config.h does not define it, so the frozen table could not
# decide it and `check-cond-eval.py src/alloc.c` reported `4 disagreements`, all of them
# `! USE_LSB_TAG` answered True by the evaluator and False by clang.  Measured the same way
# gen-cond-macros.py measures every row (the probe includes config.h first): the `#else` branch
# is the live one, so the value is that expression.
